veterans_benefits_authority.description: The Aid & Attendance Pension Supplement is one of the most valuable financial support programs available to Veterans and surviving spouses who need help with long-term care. This enhanced monthly payment is added on top of the standard VA pension and can significantly offset the cost of assisted living, memory care, in-home caregivers, or skilled personal care services.
eligibility_criteria: Require help with Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) such as bathing, dressing, eating, grooming, toileting, or adjusting prosthetic devices.
Need assistance to avoid common hazards (e.g., preventing falls, managing medications).
Bedridden due to illness or medical conditions.
Resident of a nursing home or memory-care facility due to physical or mental incapacity.
Severe visual impairment (corrected vision of 5/200 or worse in both eyes, or significant visual field loss).
Eligibility is ultimately determined by clinical need, functional ability, and income thresholds.
why_it_matters: Helps cover caregiver wages in the home.
Supports the move into assisted living or dementia care.
Offsets the cost of safety supervision for Veterans with cognitive decline.
Provides long-term financial stability for surviving spouses.
veterans_benefits_authority.why_explore: Many families do not realize that Aid & Attendance exists until after they have already spent years paying out of pocket for senior care. The application process requires medical documentation, care-provider statements, and financial records, but the payoff can be substantial. Veterans with serious medical needs may receive hundreds or even thousands of dollars per month in additional support.
veterans_benefits_authority.notes: Cannot be combined with the Housebound Allowance. Veterans must qualify for one or the other.

veterans_benefits_authority.description: An increased pension amount for Veterans or surviving spouses who are substantially confined to their home or immediate premises because of a permanent disability.
eligibility_criteria: Must already be eligible for and receiving a VA pension.
Must have a single permanent disability rated 100% disabling AND be permanently housebound.
Alternatively eligible if a 100% disability is combined with other disabilities totaling at least 60%.
The Veteran must remain substantially confined to their dwelling and immediate premises.
Eligibility is based on disability severity and clinical need.
veterans_benefits_authority.notes: Cannot be received concurrently with the Aid & Attendance Allowance.

veterans_benefits_authority.description: A Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) program that allows Veterans of all ages to manage their own long-term care budget and hire caregivers of their choice, including family members.
eligibility_criteria: Must be enrolled in VA health care.
Must require nursing-home-level care or significant assistance with daily living.
Must be clinically eligible for community-based long-term services.
Must live in an area where Veteran Directed Care is offered.
Veteran must be willing to participate in a consumer-directed care model.
veterans_benefits_authority.notes: Provides autonomy and flexibility by granting Veterans control over their care budget.

veterans_benefits_authority.description: A suite of Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) available under the VA Medical Benefits Package to help Veterans remain independent or receive skilled care.
services_include: Homemaker and Home Health Aide Care
eligibility_criteria: Must be enrolled in VA health care.
Eligibility is based on clinical need and functional status.
Services vary by local availability and medical center resources.
May require evaluation by a VA provider to determine appropriate level of care.
veterans_benefits_authority.notes: The VA does not pay for room and board in assisted living or other residential settings, but Veterans may receive GEC services while residing in such facilities.

veterans_benefits_authority.description: VA-operated nursing homes that provide rehabilitative care, skilled nursing, long-term residential care, palliative support, and hospice care.
eligibility_criteria: Must be enrolled in the VA health system.
Must be medically and psychiatrically stable.
Eligibility determined by clinical need, service-connected disability rating, income, and availability of services.
Copayments may apply for long-term stays (typically after day 21).
Hospice care is provided with no copayment.
veterans_benefits_authority.notes: Community Living Centers specialize in rehabilitation, long-term care, and end-of-life support.
